headline: Controversy: PM asks Ishraque Hossain to resign from cabinet
summary: State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain is reportedly asked to step down following a controversial anti-drug drive involving weapons.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has reportedly directed State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain to resign from the cabinet.
The move comes after Ishraque Hossain sparked controversy by personally leading an anti-drug operation with a firearm in hand.
However, the State Minister's office and Ishraque himself have denied these reports, calling them 'baseless' and 'rumors'.
The Daily Star reports that the fate of the State Minister remains uncertain as the conflict between reports and official denials continues.
caption:
Did the Prime Minister order the State Minister to resign? Conflicting reports emerge over Ishraque Hossain's fate.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has reportedly directed State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain to resign from the cabinet.

The move comes after Ishraque Hossain sparked controversy by personally leading an anti-drug operation with a firearm in hand.

However, the State Minister's office and Ishraque himself have denied these reports, calling them 'baseless' and 'rumors'.

The Daily Star reports that the fate of the State Minister remains uncertain as the conflict between reports and official denials continues.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV, The Daily Star

headline_marked: ACC [[approves charge sheet against Saima Wazed]] over WHO post
headline: ACC approves charge sheet against Saima Wazed over WHO post
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission alleges she provided false information in her CV to secure the regional director position for the WHO’s South-East Asia region.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has approved a charge sheet against Saima Wazed, daughter of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, for allegedly providing false information in her CV.
The investigation claims Saima falsely stated she worked as an honorary specialist or expert at Bangladesh Medical University, formerly known as Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University Hospital.
According to the ACC, she used this false information and abused her power to secure the post of regional director for the WHO’s South-East Asia region.
The probe further alleges that she exerted pressure to have her CV forwarded to the WHO headquarters in Geneva via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, bypassing required official files and verification.
The case was filed with the ACC’s Dhaka-1 integrated district office on March 20, 2025, and was investigated by Tahasina Munabil Haque of the Money Laundering-1 branch.
At the time of her application, Saima was the chairperson of the Suchona Foundation and the National Advisory Committee on Autism and Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
caption:
ACC approves charge sheet against Saima Wazed for allegedly using a fake CV to secure a WHO regional director post.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has approved a charge sheet against Saima Wazed, daughter of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, for allegedly providing false information in her CV.

The investigation claims Saima falsely stated she worked as an honorary specialist or expert at Bangladesh Medical University, formerly known as Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University Hospital.

According to the ACC, she used this false information and abused her power to secure the post of regional director for the WHO’s South-East Asia region.

The probe further alleges that she exerted pressure to have her CV forwarded to the WHO headquarters in Geneva via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, bypassing required official files and verification.

The case was filed with the ACC’s Dhaka-1 integrated district office on March 20, 2025, and was investigated by Tahasina Munabil Haque of the Money Laundering-1 branch.

At the time of her application, Saima was the chairperson of the Suchona Foundation and the National Advisory Committee on Autism and Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
